title: Anglicans, Lutherans and Methodists
tagline: Dialogue with mainline Christians, using Ut Unum Sint, ARCIC and the Joint Declaration as reference points.
whyItMatters: Mainline Christians share much of our worship and history, and the Church has a long record of formal dialogue with them. Knowing it helps you be honest about both agreement and real differences.

mindset.tip: Ask which tradition the person belongs to: Anglo-Catholic, evangelical, liberal or something else. Mainline churches are not all alike. (1 Peter 3:15-16)
Start with shared baptism and prayer: the Church counts baptized Christians as brothers and sisters. (CCC 818, 838; Unitatis Redintegratio 3)
Use dialogue texts honestly: the ARCIC and Lutheran documents are agreements of commissions, not final teaching of either Church.
Read their own standards, such as the Prayer Book and the Augsburg Confession, before you describe what they believe.
Be honest about hard differences, such as ordination and authority, while working together for the poor and for life. (CCC 821)

resources.title: The Book of Common Prayer
resources.creator: Church of England
resources.why: The prayer book that has shaped Anglican worship, with the Church of England's own introduction.
resources.note: The other side's own voice (Church of England)

resources.title: What We Believe
resources.creator: The Episcopal Church
resources.why: The Episcopal Church's short statement of its beliefs.
resources.note: The other side's own voice (Anglican, USA)

resources.title: The Articles of Religion of the Methodist Church
resources.creator: The United Methodist Church
resources.why: Methodist doctrinal standards in their own words.

resources.title: The Small Catechism
resources.creator: Martin Luther (Book of Concord)
resources.why: Luther's short teaching on the Creed, the Commandments and the sacraments, still used by Lutherans.

resources.title: Unitatis Redintegratio (Decree on Ecumenism)
resources.creator: Second Vatican Council
resources.why: The Council's teaching on other Christians, including the Anglican and Protestant communities.

resources.title: Ut Unum Sint
resources.creator: Pope John Paul II
resources.why: The pope commits the Catholic Church to the search for unity and to dialogue.

resources.title: Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification (1999)
resources.creator: Lutheran World Federation and the Catholic Church
resources.why: A landmark agreement that the old Catholic-Lutheran condemnations on justification no longer apply to the teaching of the partners.
resources.note: Hosted on EWTN; later joined by the World Methodist Council

resources.title: Anglican Communion: dialogue documents
resources.creator: Dicastery for Promoting Christian Unity
resources.why: The Vatican's page for the Anglican-Catholic dialogue and its documents (ARCIC and others).

resources.title: The Gift of Authority (ARCIC II, 1999)
resources.creator: Anglican-Roman Catholic International Commission
resources.why: An agreed statement on authority in the Church, including the role of the bishop of Rome.
resources.note: Commission statement, not an official teaching of either Church

resources.title: Episcopalians and the Real Presence
resources.creator: Catholic Answers
resources.why: A Catholic Q&A on how Anglican and Catholic teaching on the Eucharist compare.

resources.title: Declaration on the Way: Church, Ministry, and Eucharist
resources.creator: Catholic and Lutheran bishops of the United States (USCCB and ELCA)
resources.why: Thirty-two points of agreement on church, ministry and Eucharist, and the differences that remain.
resources.note: Joint statement (2015) from Augsburg Fortress; a PDF

resources.title: A Commentary on The Gift of Authority
resources.creator: William Henn (Pontifical Council for Promoting Christian Unity)
resources.why: A Catholic theologian explains the structure and aims of the ARCIC statement.

resources.title: Apostolicae Curae (1896)
resources.creator: Pope Leo XIII
resources.why: The pope's judgement on Anglican ordinations, which still shapes the conversation on ministry.
resources.note: Papal document, hosted on New Advent

resources.title: Anglicanorum Coetuum
resources.creator: Pope Benedict XVI
resources.why: The constitution that lets groups of Anglicans enter full communion and keep their traditions.

resources.title: The Augsburg Confession
resources.creator: Lutheran Church (Book of Concord)
resources.why: The founding Lutheran confession, a key reference for Catholic-Lutheran dialogue.
